content.user_title: Build x402 Payments for HTTP APIs
content.value_statement: HTTP APIs need a standard way to request small, per-call payments. This skill prepares and explains custody-free x402 payment flows and server payment requirements.
actual_capabilities: Decode a 402 payment response or X-PAYMENT header into payment details.
Build unsigned EIP-3009 typed data for a payer wallet to sign.
Assemble an X-PAYMENT header from payment requirements and a signature.
Call facilitator supported, verify, and settle operations.
Create PaymentRequirements and an HTTP 402 response for an API endpoint.
Fetch an x402 endpoint and return unsigned payment data when payment is required.
limitations: Supports documented EIP-3009 flows, including USDC on Base and Base Sepolia.
Does not hold private keys or sign transactions for a user.
Requires a compatible wallet to sign typed payment data.
Does not guarantee that an external API or facilitator is trustworthy.

use_cases.title: Pay a protected API
use_cases.description: Inspect a 402 challenge, sign approved typed data, and retry with an X-PAYMENT header.

use_cases.title: Monetize an API endpoint
use_cases.description: Generate payment requirements and an HTTP 402 response for a paid endpoint.

use_cases.title: Validate settlement requests

prompt_templates.title: Decode a payment request
prompt_templates.prompt: Decode this x402 HTTP 402 response. Show token, amount, recipient, network, and expiry before I pay.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a payment
prompt_templates.prompt: For this x402 payment requirement, build unsigned EIP-3009 typed data for my Base USDC wallet. Do not sign it.

prompt_templates.title: Complete paid API request
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this x402 endpoint. If it returns 402, explain payment details, prepare unsigned typed data, then tell me how to retry after I provide a signature.

prompt_templates.title: Configure API charges
prompt_templates.prompt: Create x402 PaymentRequirements for a Base API endpoint charging 0.01 USDC to this recipient. Explain how to return the HTTP 402 response and verify payment.

output: Recipient and expiry displayed for review before signing.

Required X-PAYMENT header fields after a signature is supplied.

output_examples.input: Create requirements for a paid API route.
output: Guidance for returning HTTP 402 and verifying settlement through a facilitator.

best_practices: Decode and review token, amount, recipient, network, and expiry before signing.
Use a wallet that clearly displays EIP-712 typed data before approval.
Verify a facilitator supports required network and asset before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not sign payment data without confirming recipient and amount.
Do not treat external endpoint or facilitator responses as trusted by default.
Do not use this skill as a substitute for wallet security or API authorization.

faq.question: What is x402?
faq.answer: x402 uses HTTP 402 responses to communicate payment requirements for an API request.

faq.question: Does this skill hold private keys?
faq.answer: No. It builds unsigned typed data and payment headers. Your wallet signs the authorization.

faq.question: Which token and network are documented?
faq.answer: USDC on Base and Base Sepolia are documented as known EIP-3009 token options.

faq.question: Can I use it for my API?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create payment requirements and describe how to return an HTTP 402 response.

faq.question: What does a facilitator do?
faq.answer: A facilitator can report support, verify a payment, and settle a signed authorization.

faq.question: Should I trust every payment request?
faq.answer: No. Review payment details and trust boundaries before signing or sending a paid request.
